macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures fall as AI concerns and hawkish Fed signals weigh
items.summary: U.S. stock futures declined, with Dow futures down about 0.2%, S&P 500 futures down 0.76% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.63%. Investor sentiment weakened after Anthropic shares retreated following their blockbuster debut and as traders reacted to signals that the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates again.[1]

items.title: U.S. stocks extend six-session sell-off
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 2%, the Dow dropped 2.2% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 2.2%. AI-related shares led losses, including AMD, Nvidia, SoftBank, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, while concerns about technology valuations and China exposure intensified.[2]

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations rise amid inflation concerns
items.summary: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said the central bank would need to raise interest rates again because inflation remains too high. Markets were pricing in a 98.4% probability of a rate hike at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME FedWatch.[1]

items.title: U.S. economic data show weaker manufacturing and firmer prices
items.summary: The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9, while new orders slipped into contraction and prices paid increased sharply. Initial jobless claims rose by 1,000 to 203,000, and continuing claims increased by 70,000 to 1.763 million.[2]

items.title: Oil prices decline on supply-surplus expectations
items.summary: Brent crude fell 1.6% and was headed for a third consecutive weekly decline as expectations of a supply surplus grew. Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz reportedly returned to approximately prewar levels.[1]

items.title: Asian technology stocks sell off
items.summary: Asian markets faced broad risk aversion as AI-related concerns, Federal Reserve tightening expectations and liquidity pressures intensified. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell more than 6%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index declined nearly 2%.[2][6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 as crypto liquidations surge
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000, while ether, XRP and Solana also declined. About $1.5 billion in crypto derivatives positions were liquidated over 24 hours.

items.title: Major cryptocurrencies extend losses amid market weakness
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 2.6% to roughly $61,734, ether declined 3.7%, and Solana dropped 2.5% over 24 hours. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $306.5 million in net withdrawals on November 18.

items.title: Hong Kong proposes broader virtual-asset licensing rules
items.summary: A proposed Hong Kong bill would require businesses dealing in, advising on, managing or safeguarding virtual assets to obtain a license or register with the Securities and Futures Commission. Banks supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would also need registration before offering those services.

items.title: CFTC outlines pathway for blockchain-based derivatives venues
items.summary: CFTC Chair Michael Selig said blockchain-based platforms could enter the U.S. retail derivatives market by obtaining exchange registration or partnering with an already registered venue.

items.title: Singapore reports S$100 million tokenized central-bank bill issuance
items.summary: Singapore’s monetary authority issued S$100 million of tokenized four-week central-bank bills recorded on a distributed ledger and settled using wholesale central-bank digital currency. Officials plan to expand the program and test the bills as collateral in 2027.

items.title: Polygon activates Purley network upgrade
items.summary: Polygon deployed its Purley upgrade on mainnet, adding stronger bridge-event confirmation requirements and additional validator signature checks.

items.title: Sky reports more than $2 billion in USDS redemptions
items.summary: Users exchanged more than $2 billion of Sky’s USDS stablecoin for USDC on November 19, marking a significant one-day redemption event.

items.title: Wagyu’s XMR1 token collapses after reported theft
items.summary: Wagyu’s XMR1 token plunged from nearly $500 to about $0.65 after its founder described a $13 million theft.

items.title: Binance-linked theft wallets move nearly 197,460 ETH
items.summary: Elliptic reported that wallets linked to October’s Binance theft moved approximately 197,460 ether on November 20, renewing concerns about the laundering of stolen assets.

items.title: Binance adds monitoring labels to six tokens
items.summary: Binance placed Harmony, Zilliqa, BANK, INIT, MITO and THE under its monitoring label, signaling heightened review of those assets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned for complex software, knowledge-work and scientific tasks. It offers a one-million-token context window and is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding coding, research and document work, alongside GPT-6.2 Sol for lower-cost everyday use. The launches emphasize stronger professional performance and reduced pricing compared with earlier models.

items.title: Microsoft unveils specialized MAI models
items.summary: Microsoft announced a suite of models for coding, cybersecurity and structured decision-making, including MAI Code 2. The company said its coding model approaches leading competitors’ performance at substantially lower cost.

items.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
items.summary: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max as its most capable model, marketed as more efficient and available to developers through the company’s cloud platform. Reports describe the model as significantly cheaper per task than its predecessor.

items.title: Anthropic begins public trading after IPO
items.summary: Anthropic, the developer of Claude, began trading publicly under the ticker ANT after pricing its initial public offering. Its shares reportedly closed the first day at $97.17, above the $83 offering price.

items.title: OpenAI reports AI-assisted chip-design gains
items.summary: OpenAI said its models rewrote chip-circuit code to achieve up to a 14% improvement across power, performance and area on a flagship GPU. The company also said the approach has been applied to a custom chip and used by AMD in a design sent to manufacturing.

items.title: Tencent warns export restrictions could delay its next model
items.summary: Tencent said tighter US restrictions on Chinese access to overseas data centers and advanced Nvidia hardware could delay development of its next large language model. The company expects greater reliance on domestically produced semiconductors.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI sets record with $3.79 billion first-day sales
items.summary: Rockstar Games reported that Grand Theft Auto VI generated an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on its first day, making it the largest entertainment launch ever. The company also said the game had 32.5 million pre-orders before release.

items.title: Rockstar employees vote on union recognition
items.summary: More than 1,600 Rockstar employees in the United Kingdom are reportedly voting through November 26 on whether the company should formally recognize the Rockstar Game Workers Union, affiliated with the IWGB.

items.title: Ubisoft reports weaker bookings and announces job cuts
items.summary: Ubisoft reported first-half net bookings of about €644.7 million, down roughly 16.5% year over year, lowered its third-quarter bookings outlook, and confirmed 166 job cuts in Montreal and Quebec City. The company also announced Motherbrain, an AI-focused subsidiary spun out of its Teammates prototype team.

items.title: Riot announces major League of Legends overhaul for 2027
items.summary: Riot Games unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn with a debut trailer and announced a substantial overhaul planned for 2027.

items.title: Dplus KIA signs Doran and Kanavi for 2027
items.summary: Dplus KIA announced the signing of top laner Choi “Doran” Hyeon-joon and jungler Seo “Kanavi” Jin-hyeok for its 2027 League of Legends roster. KT Rolster separately confirmed support player Kellin through the 2028 season.

items.title: Xbox Helix described as a console that can play PC games
items.summary: Microsoft said its next-generation Xbox Helix will remain a console rather than a PC, while supporting access to players’ PC game libraries.

items.title: Rainbow Six: Vegas reportedly returning
items.summary: A new installment in Ubisoft’s Rainbow Six: Vegas series was reportedly in development, according to gaming-industry coverage published Friday.
